atpl1:d970973944e15ae69ffa5dec3e819126.note: Support gradient step 1 of 5, most supported: the caregiver performs the action, so the referent is live and shared. VERB SET IS CONSTRAINED BY A MACHINE RULE, NOT BY CLINICAL CHOICE: the content validator treats jump, hop, toss, throw, catch, race and climb as critical failures in any language card, so this card uses eating, washing and reading instead. Confirm that a verb set without those is clinically adequate for action labeling; if a blocked verb is clinically necessary, say so and it will be raised as a separate decision rather than worked around.

atpl1:99eb7ec785da7ba1fb85ffe9972a0662.note: Support gradient step 2 of 5: the child's own action, which is the easiest referent after the caregiver's. Review focus: whether interrupting a child's own play to ask a question is appropriate here, and whether the natural-pause instruction is sufficient protection.

atpl1:0874e5c5a23ae528e47b27bf5f38fce9.note: Support gradient step 3 of 5: a still image, but of familiar people. Review focus: whether family photos are a clinically useful intermediate step between live action and book pictures, or whether they add nothing over a book page.

atpl1:e7cc3a3e61ff9161939bc1124bfe9b79.note: Support gradient step 4 of 5, and the milestone's OWN context: the canonical rung text names a picture or book. Review focus: page count, and whether one character per page is the right level of selectivity.

atpl1:493c8827f98983d85001907eff03d284.note: Support gradient step 5 of 5, least supported: two agents in one image, requiring the child to hold one action while labeling another. Review focus: whether two actions is the right ceiling for this rung, and whether the make_harder reversal (find who is doing a named action) belongs here or in a receptive family.

atpl1:69702817b90ba435e5c7b575db187291.note: Anchored at the 12m person-naming rung. Review focus: is a familiar-person name the right first target here, and is the arrival/departure moment frequent enough to be practicable?

atpl1:c04d588bb0437f1c6c56db0a000ea1b4.note: Anchored at the 12m person-naming rung, high-repetition variant. Review focus: round count and whether a reveal game competes with the naming target.

atpl1:f562e541df79bc55108f3607b75bebb4.note: 12m to 15m bridge: maximum array simplification, one item only. Review focus: the adaptation narrowed the source from a two-item choice to one item and removed 'reach' from success, because a reach is a gesture outcome rather than a first-word outcome. Confirm that narrowing.

atpl1:b9030e455771b9fc0213d75e9d00530e.note: Anchored at 15m object naming, embedded in the snack routine. Review focus: the what_to_avoid line is the load-bearing part — food must never be contingent on a word.

atpl1:7015cc812377ad0cb64e04e09ff02b90.note: 15m to 18m, embedded in bath and bedtime routines. Review focus: whether nightly repetition of one word is the right dose, and whether bedtime is an appropriate window at all.

atpl1:75020d1045c22f79ba398d154d1be321.note: 15m recast/expansion card. Its target is the CAREGIVER's response: treating an approximation as the word rather than as an error. Review focus: is this clinically distinct from 'One Word, One Thing' (simplification) or do the two collapse into one activity?

atpl1:c062d182c4ec09fd4432dc9a348cb742.note: Anchored at 18m: generalisation of a known word across contexts rather than acquisition of a new one. Review focus: whether generalisation or breadth of new words is the better 18m target.

atpl1:cdc591d639808c7ef952fb057634d515.note: PRE-VERBAL SAFETY WORDING IS CANDIDATE LANGUAGE AND NEEDS AN EXPLICIT DECISION: the positioning and supervision sentence in what_to_avoid was drafted by Track 2 and is not established guidance. Approve it, replace it, or supply standing wording. Content anchored at the 4m cooing rung, reaching down to 2m via make_easier.

atpl1:1f6ba8efea00dc1bf54d44f979aebf55.note: PRE-VERBAL SAFETY WORDING IS CANDIDATE LANGUAGE AND NEEDS AN EXPLICIT DECISION. Anchored at the 6m raspberry/tongue rung. The adaptation dropped the source card's spoken cue ('Say you try!'), which presumes verbal comprehension the 6m rung does not assume, and reduced it to model, pause, answer.

atpl1:9c8fc5e0bb249f3cc1db3f034b08e9a4.note: PRE-VERBAL SAFETY WORDING IS CANDIDATE LANGUAGE AND NEEDS AN EXPLICIT DECISION. Anchored at the 6m squealing rung (pitch and intensity range). Review focus: the loudness guidance, and whether squealing is a target a caregiver should be prompted to elicit at all.

atpl1:05904049483a92bd232d54e5944807cf.note: PRE-VERBAL SAFETY WORDING IS CANDIDATE LANGUAGE AND NEEDS AN EXPLICIT DECISION. Anchored at the 6m sound turn-taking rung. The adaptation kept the 'copy it back exactly' contingency from the source card but removed the toy, because the rung is VOCAL turn-taking rather than object-mediated turn-taking.

atpl1:be7588fa50653b56ecc1e822d8123978.note: PRE-VERBAL SAFETY WORDING IS CANDIDATE LANGUAGE AND NEEDS AN EXPLICIT DECISION. Anchored at the 9m reduplicated-babble rung. make_easier deliberately reaches down to any single vowel so the card stays safe if it is allocated to a child whose target is 4m — see README on why one family serves a 2m-to-9m span.

atpl1:84d62c7bb7803faf47361eba8e933e60.note: PRE-VERBAL SAFETY WORDING IS CANDIDATE LANGUAGE AND NEEDS AN EXPLICIT DECISION. Spans the whole band: the same sound at the same step of one daily routine. This card absorbed two earlier concepts (routine-embedded cooing and routine-embedded babble) that proved to be one activity at different rungs.
